old_caption: The video depicts a close-up view of a white plate placed on a yellow background. On the plate, there is a wooden popsicle stick with a small amount of yellowish-orange substance attached to it. The substance appears to be melting or dripping onto the plate, creating a pool of the same color around the stick. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, focusing on the plate and the melting substance. The lighting is consistent, highlighting the vibrant colors of the substance and the plate against the yellow backdrop. There are no other objects or characters present in the scene, and the video captures the gradual spread and pooling of the substance as it melts.

caption: The video depicts a white oval plate on a smooth orange-yellow background, holding a shallow pool of pale yellow liquid on the left and reddish-orange liquid on the right. A thin wooden stick lies diagonally across the pool, with a rounded yellowish gel-like dollop sitting on its middle. Throughout, the dollop steadily loses height and flattens into the surrounding liquid. Its edges blur and merge with the pool, exposing more of the stick’s shaft leading to its right-hand tip. The two-tone liquid remains present with only subtle shifts in the orange-red tint, while the plate, stick position, and background stay essentially fixed. The camera appears static, the dissolving dollop staying near the middle of the plate as the gradual change continues.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.

camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.
